author: Dewey Sim,Fan Chen
description:
Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO could complicate Washington’s China policy, widening the gap between a White House keen to steady ties with Beijing and an incoming Democratic-led Congress poised to tighten chip curbs.
The assessment from analysts comes after the AI chip giant on Monday reinstated Huang as chief executive, president and board director. The Nvidia board said it had determined – following inputs from senior US government officials – that his return did not pose a national...
title: How Jensen Huang’s Nvidia return could deepen US rift over China chip curbs

author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
At a cafe in Austin, Texas, a group gathers on a sunny Friday morning. Just a few years ago, many were strangers. Today, one has brought biscuits, another T-shirts emblazoned with “Asian Texans Vote”. They have bonded through their shared opposition to Texas Senate Bill 17 (SB17), which became law last year.
“If you have to say one positive thing about all this … it’s that I made friends with a group of people I never knew before,” says Hugh Li, president of the Austin Chinese-American Network...
title: Chinese Texans hope Democratic victories will bring relief from Senate Bill 17

author: Victoria Bela
description:
“A union together is much more powerful than each country individually,” Fields medallist Shing-Tung Yau declared after scholars from across Asia gathered in Hong Kong on Tuesday for the inauguration of the Asian Mathematical Union (AsianMU).
Participants say the initiative will unite regional talent in mathematics.
Representatives from the founding nations – China, Russia, India, Japan, South Korea and Iran – said during the ceremony that the union would help foster cross-border collaboration,...
title: Mathematicians of Asia unite: new union brings the continent’s brightest minds together

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
When Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi arrived and left the Apec host city Shenzhen last week, retired diplomat Zhang Qiyue was there on the red carpet for the greeting and send-off.
Other leaders were received by serving senior officials but Takaichi was welcomed by the 67-year-old former envoy to Belgium, Indonesia, and Greece.
Zhang is also the daughter of Zhang Shu, Beijing’s ambassador to Tokyo in the late 1980s – a deliberate choice that analysts said sent a careful message: while...
title: Why did China choose a retired diplomat to welcome Sanae Takaichi to Apec?

author: SCMP Reporter
description:
Shanghai party chief Chen Jining has been placed under investigation on suspicion of corruption, state broadcaster CCTV reported on Wednesday.
Chen, who is also a member of the Politburo, is suspected of serious breaches of discipline and law, the standard euphemism for corruption.
More to follow...
title: Shanghai party chief Chen Jining faces corruption probe

author: Liu Zhen
description:
The Chinese navy’s new carrier-based fighter trainer – the JL-15 – will be unveiled at the Zhuhai air show in southern China next month, according to state media reports.
Reports on Monday said the People’s Liberation Army Navy had confirmed that the JL-15 would be part of the line-up at the December 7-13 air show, alongside naval aircraft including the WZ-2 uncrewed helicopter.
The JL-15 is a dedicated platform to train pilots for operations on PLA aircraft carriers with electromagnetic...
title: China’s carrier-based JL-15 fighter trainer to make public debut at Zhuhai air show

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
A new nuclear bomb designation buried in a US Senate budget document suggests Washington may be pursuing a weapon to destroy targets deep underground.
The B94 designation surfaced on November 12 in an explanatory statement accompanying the US Senate Appropriations Committee’s draft energy and water funding bill for the 2027 financial year.
Listed under the National Nuclear Security Administration’s (NNSA) stockpile modernisation programme, the entry recommends US$77.1 million for the B94,...
title: US B94 nuclear bomb designation signals renewed push for bunker-busting weapons

author: Phoebe Zhang
description:
Liu Min, a senior official at the Ministry of Science and Technology, is under investigation, according to China’s top anti-corruption watchdog, the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI).
Liu is “suspected of serious violations of party discipline and national laws” – a euphemism for corruption – and is currently subject to disciplinary review by the CCDI team at the ministry.
She is also being investigated by the supervisory commission in Yichang, Hubei province, in central China,...
title: China corruption watchdog investigates senior science ministry official Liu Min

author: Victoria Bela
description:
For centuries, scholars, officials and local chroniclers in China recorded the world around them, resulting in a collection of imperial histories, gazetteers, personal diaries and records that is seen as the most continuous in the world.
Among them are detailed accounts of the weather – including droughts, floods and harvest conditions – which researchers have used to try to reconstruct and understand the region’s climate history.
But a new study by researchers in China and Germany, based on...
title: China’s historical climate records could be skewed by human bias, study finds

author: Ji Siqi
description:
China’s Tiangong space station is set to welcome its first foreign astronaut as part of the Shenzhou-24 crew announced on Tuesday.
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan’s armed forces, will join Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi aboard China’s latest crewed space mission, which is scheduled to lift off at 8.18am on Wednesday, according to Zhang Jingbo, spokesman for the China Manned Space Agency and director of its general plan bureau.
This also marks the first joint space...
title: Pakistani astronaut joins Shenzhou-24 crew heading for China’s Tiangong space station

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwan’s local elections on Saturday will test the ruling Democratic Progressive Party’s political strength, the opposition’s unity and the island’s direction ahead of the 2028 leadership race.
Voters will elect officials across 22 cities and counties. But attention is focused on Taipei and New Taipei City, where closely watched contests could have significant implications for Taiwanese leader William Lai Ching-te and main opposition Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun.
Adding an unexpected twist...
title: What’s at stake and the battlegrounds to watch as Taiwan heads to the polls
